column3: couldn't get a job at any university.
So he took a job at a patent office.
In his spare time, he wrote physics papers.
In nineteen oh five, he published four of them.
One changed how we understand time.
And one gave us the most famous equation... ever.
In nineteen nineteen, an eclipse proved his theory right.
Newspapers called it a revolution in science.
Then, he won the Nobel Prize.
Not bad... for a patent clerk.
